findings.title: T8557 Double free in GPGME read_status/read_colon_line (src/engine-gpg.c)
findings.summary_md: GnuPG's private bug task, opened on 13 November 2026 and switched to public visibility on 20 November, records the flaw in read_status() and read_colon_line() in src/engine-gpg.c. A local buffer pointer is grown with realloc() but written back to the engine context only at the end of the function; early returns from status or colon callbacks leave the context holding freed memory that is freed again when the engine is released. The task lists fix commits rM14499348b966 and rMb4358e92e33a and confirms the code was present in 1.18.0 and later distribution releases through current master.

findings.title: [Announce] GnuPG Security Advisory for GPGME (T8557,CVE-2026-129975)
findings.summary_md: Werner Koch announced GPGME 2.3.1 as the fix for CVE-2026-129975, a critical double free triggered by an OpenPGP key with a crafted very long user ID. The advisory says the bug can exfiltrate application data, for example through signed data, and that remote code execution cannot be ruled out. Johan Carlsson discovered it and GitLab notified GnuPG on 12 November; coordinated disclosure had been set for 25 November but was moved to 20 November because of a separate Ruby2Shell bug at GitLab. All software using GPGME before 2.3.0 is affected, including shared libraries, DLLs and statically linked builds, with updated Gpg4win 5.1.2 and GnuPG Desktop and VS-Desktop packages released alongside the library.

findings.title: [SECURITY] [DSA 6646-1] gpgme1.0 security update
findings.summary_md: Debian's Salvatore Bonaccorso credited Johan Carlsson with finding that GPGME mishandles OpenPGP keys with a crafted very long user ID, leading to information disclosure, denial of service and potentially arbitrary code execution. DSA-6646-1 fixed CVE-2026-129975 for stable trixie in gpgme1.0 version 1.24.2-3+deb13u1 and recommended upgrading the package. The advisory pointed users to the Debian security tracker for the broader gpgme1.0 status.

findings.title: GPGME 2.3.1 fixes critical double-free in OpenPGP key parsing
findings.summary_md: This 20 November news item covered the GPGME 2.3.1 release and CVE-2026-129975, describing the long user ID trigger, possible data theft and the 20 November disclosure. It restated GnuPG's account of the 1,024-byte status and colon-line readers, the stale pointer left by an early read failure, and the affected products including Gpg4win, GnuPG Desktop, VS-Desktop, mail and XMPP clients, Samba and Flatpak. It also reported the 12 November notification from GitLab and the disclosure moved forward from 25 November because of the separate Ruby2Shell flaw.
